old: Swedish verbs ending in -s can be passive or deponent (active meaning). Context determines which.
focus: Anchor to 'träffas': verbs in -s can be passive OR deponent/active; here träffas = meet each other. Quote the target.

english: We always succeed in the end.
old: "Lyckas" (succeed) is deponent. "I slutändan" = in the end.
focus: Lead with the surprise: lyckas ends in -s yet is active ('we succeed'), not passive – Swedish deponent verb. Drop the word 'deponent' and the 'i slutandan' gloss; quote lyckas.

old: "Skulle ha" + supine also = should have (in hindsight).
focus: Lead with the ambiguity: skulle ha stannat means both 'would have stayed' and regretful 'should have stayed' – context decides. Quote skulle ha stannat; drop the '+ supine' table talk.

target: Den stängda dörren hela tiden under sommaren.
english: The closed door all the time during summer.
old: Past participle as adjective: changes for gender! En-word: -d. Ett-word: -t. Plural: -da.
focus: Hook: unlike English, Swedish past participles inflect like adjectives. Anchor to this card's stangd/stangt/stangda (den stangda dorren); trim the paradigm-table feel.

old: Particle verbs: verb + particle (upp, ner, ut, in, av, på). The particle changes the meaning.
focus: Anchor to this card: ringa = to call, ringa upp = to phone someone back – the particle upp reshapes the verb. Quote ringer upp; drop the generic particle list.

target: Kundservicen på den där butiken är under all kritik.
english: The customer service at that shop is beneath contempt.
old: Means so bad it can't even be criticized properly.
focus: Give the literal logic and quote the phrase: under all kritik = 'below all criticism' – so bad it's beyond critiquing.

target: Han tog skeden i vacker hand.
old: To accept a difficult situation and deal with it.
focus: Give the literal image and quote it: ta skeden i vacker hand = 'take the spoon in a fair hand' = grit your teeth and make the best of a hard situation.

target: Pengar har vi inte, men tid har vi.
english: Money we don't have, but time we do.
old: Parallel fronting creates contrast between two objects.
focus: Swedish fronts the object for contrast: Pengar har vi inte, men tid har vi = 'Money we don't have, but time we do' — plain words, no 'fronting' jargon, quote pengar/tid

target: Sjunga kan hon verkligen, hon vann talangshown tre år i rad.
english: Sing she really can, she won the talent show three years in a row.
old: Verb topicalization: placing the infinitive first for emphasis.
focus: Swedish can put the bare verb first for emphasis: Sjunga kan hon = 'Sing, she really can' — plain framing, drop 'topicalization/infinitive' jargon, quote sjunga
torde is a formal modal for cautious probability ('should/presumably'): det torde vara möjligt = 'it should presumably be possible' — frame as usage, not a bare gloss

target: Minnet av sommarens dagar värmde hennes hjärta.
english: The memory of summer days warmed her heart.
old: "Sommarens" = summer's (genitive -s). Possessive -s works like English apostrophe-s.
focus: Swedish genitive is just -s with NO apostrophe (unlike English): sommarens dagar = 'summer's days' — lead with the missing-apostrophe trap, quote sommarens

target: I fjärran hördes ljudet av bjällror.
english: In the distance the sound of bells was heard.
old: "I fjärran" = in the distance (literary). "Hördes" = was heard (s-passive).
focus: past-tense s-passive: hördes = 'was heard' (-s/-des ending makes the passive) — drop the 'i fjärran' gloss, one rule only, quote hördes
